Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
**Answer:**

(a) In the worst case, a single vertex can have all |E| outgoing edges. The cost of the worst possible single operation is therefore **|E|**.

(b) Using aggregate analysis, the total cost summed over all |V| operations equals the sum of all outgoing edge counts, which equals |E|. The average amortized cost is thus **|E| / |V|**.

* The worst single operation corresponds to a vertex whose out-degree equals |E|, which is the maximum possible when all edges originate from one vertex.
* By aggregate analysis, dividing the total cost |E| by the |V| operations gives the average amortized cost of |E|/|V|, which is simply the average out-degree across the graph.
